speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for clarifying. Given your history of Kaposi's sarcoma and recent fungal esophagitis, have you noticed any skin lesions or oral ulcers appearing in the past few months? Additionally, have you had any recent exposure to new sexual partners or intravenous drug use?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis. Given your low CD4 count history, AIDS, and the classic presentation of painless decreased vision with "black spots" (hemorrhages), this is the most urgent and likely diagnosis requiring immediate antiviral treatment.
